decision: started the WR-1 run from the multi-phase plan
why: Chief gave the go in the Claude Code session

decision: asked Chief to create the public repo by hand
why: the Claude GitHub App gets 403 on POST /user/repos

decision: serve the site from main:/docs instead of a Pages workflow
why: branch publishing needs no deploy job and no extra token

decision: pinned every source to a commit and rebuilt dict and OCR files from scratch
why: a reviewer can rerun the build and get the same bytes
evidence: tools/fetch_sources.sh, cmp of dict.json and docs/ocr

decision: wrote tests/e2e.js covering the ten live lanes from the plan
why: one script reruns every lane instead of hand checks

decision: kept the handwritten list photo out of the repo
why: it is Chief's family photo and the repo is public

decision: removed 22 section banner comments from app.src.html
why: pstack no-comments keeps only comments that explain a non-obvious why; the comment-sicko agent is not loaded in this session

decision: fixed two bugs in the perf probe before trusting its numbers
why: it timed home before the page script ran and reused the same file input so the second upload never fired

decision: measured home 2.7 s, first photo 22.6 s, warm photo 0.9 s on Moto G4, 4x CPU, Fast 3G, gzip
why: plan budgets are 4, 40 and 8 seconds
result: pass; first photo is bound by downloading about 5 MB gzip of OCR files; CPU throttling does not reach the worker so warm time is optimistic

decision: photo upload failed on Chief's second Android phone; same photo works in emulated Chromium
why: cannot see the phone's error, so the page now shows the failing stage and error text
evidence: local run of the 2592x4608 photo recognized 6 words with no error

decision: started WR-4 on a branch stacked on WR-1
why: Chief asked to start WR-4 after the browser prototype

decision: pinned PP-OCRv6 small from the rapidocr 3.10.0 wheel and onnxruntime-web 1.30.0 by sha256
why: 1.31.1 was under two weeks old; the wheel ships the models with Apache-2.0 notes

decision: trim short unknown tokens at the ends of photo lines
why: PaddleOCR reads the Chinese meaning next to pins as a stray E and the whole line was dropped

decision: compare the photo word lists without order in tests/e2e.js
why: PaddleOCR reads the two-column sheet row by row and the quiz shuffles anyway

decision: throttle the network in the perf server instead of DevTools
why: DevTools network emulation never finished the worker's large model fetches, even after 20 minutes

decision: WR-4 on Moto G4, 4x CPU, Fast 3G: home 3.0 s, first photo 167.3 s, later photos 3.5 s
why: plan budgets 4, 180 and 15 s; 30 MB gzip at 1.44 Mbit/s needs about 160 s, so the first photo is bound by download
evidence: node tests/perf.js 3, ranges 3.0-3.3, 167.2-168.2, 3.1-3.5; WR-1 rerun with the same probe: 3.1, 22.8, 1.1

decision: started WR-5, the hero adventure theme
why: the child asked for a second adventure; Chief approved the art and shared records

decision: put all theme art and words in one THEMES table and kept one practice flow
why: every feature must stay in both adventures, so the flow cannot fork

decision: kept one shared record; a finished list shows as a planet or a medal
why: Chief chose shared records
result: hero lane checks the count after switching

decision: page network-first, recognition files cache-first and only after the first photo
why: a new deploy reaches the child as soon as the tablet is online, and the 30 MB download is not forced on first open
result: e2e offline lane passes, including offline photo recognition

decision: kept the photo button name; added hints for few words, a missing voice and in-app browsers
why: PaddleOCR now reads handwriting, so the plan's rename to printed-only no longer fits; the other three are what the phone tests ran into

decision: added a third theme in original blocky pixel art instead of copying the game the child named
why: the repo is public and that game's name and characters are trademarked

decision: normalize answers with NFKC and drop invisible characters
why: Chief saw bowling bumpers marked wrong while it looked right; full-width letters and zero-width characters both reproduce that
